question: Does a learned bounded transition predictor improve changed-assumption planning beyond ordinary preconditions and sequence validation?
reference: Existing Eva C fallback, ordinary reusable-method artifact, full current contract, current-state reads, sequence-on-copy validation, preserved stop/audience/request identity boundaries.
candidate: One model-generated, version-1 transition predictor with explicit unsupported/unknown results. The same reasoning owner selects all real fixture actions.
ablation: Candidate artifact disabled; identical to the ordinary-method arm by construction. No extra baseline arm.
generation: One combined ordinary-method/predictor synthesis from the public contract and development transitions only; gpt-6-astra medium, existing subscription route. No hidden case access.
heldout: Independently curated cases A and B, repeated twice in each of two arms; candidate frozen before inputs are released.
hard: No production state or house actions

budget.includes: Synthesis, development validation, both arms, social contact calls, repairs and all recorded helpers. No arbitrary elapsed-time pause is introduced.

decision: Promote only under the existing learning-and-initiative section9 gate; otherwise reject or retain unknown evidence. Do not turn equivalent results into a technical-innovation claim.
accounting: Raw attested usage per response, cached input separately, actual service reads/writes/validation/prediction calls, construction and maintenance. No claim of amortized savings without five represented eligible uses.
scope: An isolated fixture decision, not the installed Eva, complete competitor comparison or family acceptance.
prior_art: Existing technical-differentiation research, including Twin; no superiority claim against an unrun or unavailable implementation.
